Deepak Gupta, J.
One

Anil Kumar of village Kamod, Tehsil Charkhi Dadri lost his life in a motor vehicular accident,
which took place on 05.12.2015.
His widow, minor children and parents filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation against the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

2. Learned Tribunal vide award dated 30.08.2017 assessed the compensation of 14,21,000/-
payable by all the respondents along with interest.
3. Seeking enhancement, the present appeal has been filed, accompanied by application bearing CM No. 13367 13367-CII of 2022 so as to condone the delay of 993 days in filing the appeal.
4. It is submitted that after passing passing of the award on 30.08.2017, the counsel of the appellants did not inform them.
The appellants approached their counsel in December, 2017 and came to know that their claim petition had been allowed.
They were under bonafide impression that there was no limitation to file the appeal before High Court and for this reason, they did not contact their counsel immediately.

Later on, Covid-19 Covid 19 pandemic set in and after contacting Page N:
1 of 2 1 of 2 the counsel at Chandigarh, they came to know that limitation period to file the appeal eal was 90 days and then they swung into action to file this appeal.
It is contended that in the circumstances, delay of 993 days be condoned.

sentences.text: 1 5. The reasons projected to condone the delay do not inspire confi- conf dence.
The plea that they were unaware of the fact that there is no limitation to file the appeal is wholly vague.
The appellants were admittedly represented by counsel before the Tribunal, as reflected in the award itself.
Once the award was passed on 30.08.2017, the appellants were expected to act with reasonable dili- dil gence.
A litigant who is already in the company of legal representation cannot later plead complete ignorance of legal remedies or "technicalities of law" as a ground for condonation.

6. The law is well-settled well settled that "sufficient ccause"
ause" under Section 5 of the Limitation Act must be bona fide, reasonable, and must explain the entire period of delay.
Negligence, inaction, or lack of diligence cannot be condoned merely on sympathetic considerations.

The Supreme Court has repeatedly hel heldd that limitation cannot be extended on the basis of vague assertions or afterthoughts and that the Court must balance the rights accrued to the other side due to expiry of limitation.
7. In the present case, the appellants have failed to satisfacto satisfactorily rily ex- e plain even a fraction of the 993-day 993 day delay.
Their explanation is neither plausible nor supported by any material.
The delay, being inordinate and unexplained, cannot be condoned.
8. Accordingly, the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Ac Actt is dismissed.
As a necessary consequence, the appeal, being barred by limitation, also stands dismissed.
All pending miscellaneous applications, if any, stand disposed of.
(DEEPAK GUPTA)
